name: Ivy Framework
desc: The ultimate framework for building internal tools with LLM code generation — front-end and back-end unified into a single C# codebase.
role: Founding engineer and top contributor. Own the core codebase, product engineering and the AI code-generation model that turns prompts into working C# apps.

name: Ivy Tendril
desc: What replaces your IDE in an agentic era — a developer tool built for when agents write 99% of the code and your job is knowing what good looks like.
role: Led design and implementation from the first commit. 2,000 commits and 650+ PRs in under six months.

name: SpaceCorps 2
desc: WebGL-based 3D MMO RPG that runs in the browser — client and server. The project that became a company.
role: Founder & CEO. Spotted the gap for an open-source browser MMO, built the prototype solo, then recruited and led an international team of six.

name: SpaceCorps Front
desc: The production front-end for SpaceCorps — three.js/WebGL rendering, real-time multiplayer state, and the full game client shell.
role: Architected the rendering and networking layers, and ran the team delivering toward the 2026 launch.

name: GrowthHack
desc: Growth and distribution tooling built at SpaceCorps — 424 commits in three months.
role: Built end to end, from data pipeline through to the operator-facing UI.

name: Rusty Framework
desc: Build full-stack web applications in pure Rust — a direct port of Ivy-Framework to a systems language.
role: Ported the framework's architecture into Rust to test how far the single-language full-stack idea travels outside .NET.

name: RustMC Server
desc: A multi-threaded Minecraft server written in Rust with Paper plugin compatibility.
role: Side project turned performance study: concurrency, protocol implementation, and binary compatibility with an existing plugin ecosystem.

name: Ivy Examples
desc: Community-created full-stack C# application demos built on Ivy-Framework.
role: Curate and author the reference applications that show developers what the framework can do.

name: Ivy Command Center
desc: Permission-based access control for Ivy apps.
role: Designed and shipped the authorization layer — roles, policies and per-app permission scoping.

name: timup.pro
desc: Production .NET web platform shipped with a team during the SALT full-stack programme.
role: Team build under mob-programming and TDD discipline — ASP.NET, EF Core, CI/CD, deployed live.

name: KeepIn
desc: Inventory, messaging and handling system for e-commerce businesses, with 3D storage visualisation.
role: Full-stack build: C# API, React front-end, and a WebGL view of physical warehouse space.

name: GETELEC
desc: General Tool for Electron Emission Calculations — computing emission current and Nottingham-effect heat, used in collaboration with CERN.
role: Built the online interface bridging theoretical and experimental physics. Basis of my first-author IEEE IVNC 2023 paper.

name: open-apple-models
desc: Real tool calling for Apple's on-device Foundation Models — NPC dialogue, AI decisions and content generation for games on iOS, iPadOS, macOS and visionOS 27, with no API keys or server costs.
role: In our tests Apple's own fm serve returned 0 tool calls in 54 requests, so I built per-step tool steering, a Swift package, the oam CLI, an OpenAI-compatible server and a JSON-RPC protocol with a C ABI for game engines.

name: open-android-models
desc: The Android sibling on Gemini Nano via ML Kit's GenAI Prompt API. Same concepts and same JSON-RPC protocol, so a game engine can inject either backend per platform.
role: Gemini Nano has no native tool calling yet, so I built a validated step-envelope tool loop in Kotlin, plus a JNI entry point for native engines. Pre-release: tested on the JVM and against Apple's model as a proxy, not yet on a Gemini Nano device.
